cases.sentence: От дома князя Щербатова пленных повели прямо вниз по ___, левее Девичьего монастыря и подвели к огороду, на котором стоял столб.
cases.explain: «Девичьему полю» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: From Prince Shcherbátov’s house the prisoners were led straight down the Virgin’s Field, to the left of the nunnery, as far as a kitchen garden in which a post had been set up. Beyond that post a fresh pit had been dug in the ground, and near the post and the pit a large crowd stood in a semicircle. The crowd consisted of a few Russians and many of Napoleon’s soldiers who were not on duty—Germans, Italians, and Frenchmen, in a variety of uniforms. To the right and left of the post stood rows of French troops in blue uniforms with red epaulets and high boots and shakos.

cases.sentence: За столбом была вырыта ___ с свеже-выкопанною землей, и около ямы и столба полукругом стояла большая толпа народа.
cases.explain: «большая яма» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Справа и слева столба стояли фронты ___ в синих мундирах с красными эполетами, в штиблетах и киверах.
cases.explain: «французских войск» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Преступников расставили по ___, который был в списке (Пьер стоял шестым), и подвели к столбу.
cases.explain: «известному порядку» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The prisoners were placed in a certain order, according to the list (Pierre was sixth), and were led to the post. Several drums suddenly began to beat on both sides of them, and at that sound Pierre felt as if part of his soul had been torn away. He lost the power of thinking or understanding. He could only hear and see. And he had only one wish—that the frightful thing that had to happen should happen quickly. Pierre looked round at his fellow prisoners and scrutinized them.

cases.explain: «старший офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Pierre heard the French consulting whether to shoot them separately or two at a time. “In couples,” replied the officer in command in a calm voice. There was a stir in the ranks of the soldiers and it was evident that they were all hurrying—not as men hurry to do something they understand, but as people hurry to finish a necessary but unpleasant and incomprehensible task.

cases.sentence: Чиновник-француз в шарфе подошел к ___ шеренги преступников и прочел по-русски и по-французски приговор.
cases.explain: «правой стороне» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: A French official wearing a scarf came up to the right of the row of prisoners and read out the sentence in Russian and in French.

cases.sentence: Вдруг послышался треск и грохот, показавшиеся Пьеру громче самых ___ грома, и он оглянулся.
cases.explain: «страшных ударов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Twelve sharpshooters with muskets stepped out of the ranks with a firm regular tread and halted eight paces from the post. Pierre turned away to avoid seeing what was going to happen. Suddenly a crackling, rolling noise was heard which seemed to him louder than the most terrific thunder, and he looked round. There was some smoke, and the Frenchmen were doing something near the pit, with pale faces and trembling hands. Two more prisoners were led up. In the same way and with similar looks, these two glanced vainly at the onlookers with only a silent appeal for protection in their eyes, evidently unable to understand or believe what was going to happen to them. They could not believe it because they alone knew what their life meant to them, and so they neither understood nor believed that it could be taken from them.

cases.sentence: Был дым, и французы с ___ и дрожащими руками что-то делали у ямы.
cases.explain: «бледными лицами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: То ли он понял, что напрасно кричать, или то, что невозможно, чтоб его убили люди, но он стал у столба, ожидая повязки вместе с другими, и как подстреленный зверь оглядываясь вокруг себя ___.
cases.explain: «блестящими глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: (Pierre shuddered and shook himself free.) The lad was unable to walk. They dragged him along, holding him up under the arms, and he screamed. When they got him to the post he grew quiet, as if he suddenly understood something. Whether he understood that screaming was useless or whether he thought it incredible that men should kill him, at any rate he took his stand at the post, waiting to be blindfolded like the others, and like a wounded animal looked around him with glittering eyes.
